How the value is exposed to assistive technology and updated without spamming
When the work finishes, and how completion differs from success
What the reader can do while waiting, including cancelling
How long is too long, and what replaces the bar then

rules.statement: A determinate bar only appears when the value is real; an invented percentage that jumps from 90% to waiting is worse than an indeterminate spinner.
The bar is role=progressbar with aria-valuenow/min/max, and updates are throttled to at most one announcement per second so a screen reader is not flooded.
Reaching 100% means the work ended, not that it succeeded; the outcome (passed, failed, partially applied) is stated in text afterwards.
Anything longer than two seconds offers cancel, and cancelling states what remains (nothing, or a partial result) rather than silently stopping.
Work longer than about ten seconds becomes a job with its own state the reader can leave and return to, instead of a bar that owns the page.

stateMachine.staleResponseRule: progress values are monotonic per run id; a value from an earlier run is discarded so a restart never shows a bar moving backwards, and the fill is driven by the value rather than by a second state

sections.intent: Tell the reader that work is happening, how much is left when that is knowable, and what happened when it stopped.
useCases: see that a save is in flight
nicheDifferences: Progress is a promise about time, and a fake bar breaks trust more than a spinner does
The honest split is determinate when the total is known, indeterminate otherwise
inputs: whether a total exists and is stable
how long the work typically takes
whether it can continue in the background
anatomy: a cancel action for long work
styling: a 4 px track with a single accent fill, no gradient stripes
the label sits beside, not inside, the bar
the bar does not animate when reduced-motion is set
a11y: role=progressbar with aria-valuenow/min/max and a text value
updates throttled to about one announcement per second
completion announced once with the outcome
cancel is a real button reachable before the bar
responsive: the bar keeps its width to the container at 320 px with the label wrapping below
long file names truncate in the middle above the bar
the bar never becomes a full-screen overlay
copy: completion reads 'Import finished — 1 188 rows added, 12 skipped'
cancelling reads 'Cancelled after 412 rows; nothing was saved'
alternatives: a spinner when the total is unknown
a job list when the work outlives the page
an inline status line for sub-second saves
acceptance: a determinate bar only appears with a real total
the value is exposed with aria-valuenow and announced at most about once a second
100% is followed by an outcome, not by a claim of success
work over two seconds offers cancel and says what remains
reduced-motion stops the fill animation without losing the value
failureCases: the bar jumps to 90% and waits there for a minute
the reader cancels and the partial result is silently kept
every pixel of progress is announced to the screen reader
a finished bar is treated as success although three rows failed

refused.reason: a progress bar is not interactive; the cancel action beside it carries availability
an indeterminate run has no percentage to complete; its end is an outcome, not a fill
